diagnostic: Perennial, usually monoecious, to about 3 dm; stems erect or prostrate; malpighiaceous hairs may be present but are not silvery.
Leaves petiolate, obovate to linear, margins entire; surfaces hairy or glabrous.
Short axillary bisexual racemes; staminate petals free from the androphore is an important FNA key character.
Stamens usually 10; pistillate petals very small, elliptic to filiform; styles glabrous with flattened stigmas.
Capsules hispidulous/strigillose or glabrous; seeds smooth to rugose/papillate.
morphology.learner_note: Prioritize inflorescence and floral characters over low habit or pubescence, which vary.

photos.assessment: Current herbarium specimen can support whole-plant/specimen morphology, but diagnostic field macros of staminate/pistillate flowers, capsule, and seed are still needed; iNaturalist candidates require observation-level ID/license checks.
